Artemis II was a crewed lunar flyby mission that took place from April 1 to April 11, 2026.
NASA operated the Artemis II mission as the first crewed flight of the Artemis program and the Space Launch System.
The four-person crew consisted of commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch, and mission specialist Jeremy Hansen.
Reid Wiseman was the oldest person to travel beyond low Earth orbit and around the Moon during this mission.
Victor Glover became the first person of color to travel around the Moon on this mission.
Christina Koch was the first woman to travel around the Moon on this mission.
Jeremy Hansen was the first non-American astronaut to travel around the Moon on this mission.
The Artemis II spacecraft, named Integrity by the crew, was manufactured by Lockheed Martin for the Orion module and Airbus for the European Service Module.
The mission launched from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B on April 1, 2026, at 22:35:12 UTC aboard an SLS rocket.
Artemis II reached a maximum distance of 252,756 miles from Earth, surpassing the previous record set by Apollo 13.
The crew observed a solar eclipse lasting 57 minutes while passing behind the Moon on April 6, 2026.
The mission concluded with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego on April 11, 2026.
The USS John P. Murtha recovered the crew and the Orion spacecraft after the splashdown.
NASA tested optical communications using the Orion Artemis II Optical Communications System (O2O) which achieved a downlink rate of up to 260 megabits per second.
The mission included the AVATAR payload, the first time the system was tested outside the International Space Station and Earth's Van Allen belt.
The crew's zero-gravity indicator plush toy named Rise was designed by eight-year-old Lucas Ye and displayed during the mission.
